title: Emi's office on B2
caption: The copy room is cut in two by a partition: the left part is now Emi's office with its own doorway from the corridor, and the copier keeps the right part. On day 2 Emi sits at her own desk there instead of standing in the lift lobby. Issue #238.

sections.title: Before
sections.caption: One big copy room; on day 2 Emi waited in the lift lobby.

sections.title: After
sections.caption: Her desk with a nameplate エミ / EMI, a monitor, lamp, folders and mug; a guest chair on a rug; a backlit coast panel for a window and a calendar on the wall behind her; a cabinet with a team photo and a plant, prints over a bookcase, a coat stand, a filing cabinet and a tall plant.

sections.title: Fix: Emi no longer sits through her desk (#240)
sections.caption: Jørgen: "why is she clipped into the table". People placed straight into a seat started a short blend from standing to sitting while the body was already moved back for the seat, so for that moment (and in any still or paused frame) they sat about half a metre forward, in the desk. They now go straight into the seated pose. The desks' drawer pedestals are also a little narrower, because Eric's knees went 5 cm into them at his desk. A new check (game3d/tools/seat-check.mjs) measures every seated body against the desk or table in front of it, on every seat in B2, the train and the day-2 bench.

sections.title: Emi faces the door (#241)
sections.caption: Jørgen: "can you turn emi around, it doesnt make sense to have her back to the door, and the guest seat on the inner side of the office". Her desk is turned round: she sits on the far side facing the doorway, and the guest chair is between the doorway and her desk, facing her. The window panel is now on the wall beside her, the calendar on the partition, the cabinet with the team photo behind her, and the coat stand and the bookcase with the prints by the doorway.

sections.title: Her desk is open underneath (#248)
sections.caption: Jørgen: "the desk should also be open underneath showing her legs". Her desk has no front panel now and only one drawer unit, on the side away from the doorway, with two slim legs at the other end, so her legs and feet show from the doorway and from the guest chair. The open-office desks keep both drawer units and their front panels.
